text:
support_jess: Hey team, LogiPro is seeing a sustained 429s window hitting them around 00:00-00:10 UTC. They say it started after enabling a longpoll keepalive in their SDK. Customer reports 1.5k RPM and ~18k TPM but steady errors at the edge. Posting sample headers/logs below.

devon: can you drop the request/resp headers and any x-rate-limit headers they saw? also did they change tokens or fanout?

support_jess: pasted log excerpt from their ingester: 
```
POST /v1/generate 200 OK
x-request-id: rp-9a8f
user: logipro-tenant-42
content-length: 512
received_at: 2025-10-09T00:01:12Z
-- next: 429 Too Many Requests
POST /v1/generate 429
x-request-id: rp-9a90
retry-after: 1
x-edge-rpm: 1500
x-edge-tpm: 17999
```
They also sent a curl that toggles `?wait=true` longpoll which opens a streaming connection that reconnects every 6s when idle.

alex_sre: interesting — streams that reconnect frequently can blow up RPM because each reconnect counts as a new request. if the client keeps a short reconnect interval (6s) and they have many users, effective RPM multiplies. do we have their per-token concurrency/slot usage?

support_jess: LogiPro Ops says they have ~250 active tokens and each client does a keepalive reconnect pattern. math they provided: 250 tokens * (60/6 reconnects per minute) = 2500 extra RPM, plus their normal request traffic.

maya_engineer: that math checks out. Also their client uses immediate retry on 429 without exponential backoff — they retry with a fixed 500ms delay up to 3 times. that'll amplify the problem. recommended repro: run a local script that opens N longpolls that close then reconnect every 6s and measure RPM.

devon: can you confirm whether our edge is counting longpoll reconnects as full requests (yes) and whether streaming keepalives increment the per-minute window on connect vs on token usage?

alex_sre: confirmed — connect handshake hits the rate limiter. each stream open is a request that increments the token bucket. internal metrics show a spike in token-bucket fills at ~00:00 matching their longpoll cron.

oncall_tara: tagging oncall — we can either give a temporary quota bump, recommend client fixes, or implement server-side transient smoothing. What's quickest for the customer?

support_jess: LogiPro wants immediate relief. Asked if we can throttle their reconnects server-side for 60s grace or return Retry-After longer. they also asked for guidance to change client behavior.

maya_engineer: quick mitigation options:
- issue a temporary quota increase for tenant-42 for the next 24h (fast, manual).
- mitigate on edge with a short dedupe window (treat reconnects from same token within 10s as a single RPM event) — code change and riskier.
- advise the client to switch to jittered exponential backoff + keepalive interval >= 30s and multiplex streams per token.

devon: for the support playbook, also suggest adjusting client to honor `Retry-After` header and backoff policy: `Retry-After: 5` on 429 for streaming reconns. we can push a config change on the rate limiter to return larger Retry-After for token-stream endpoints.

alex_sre: I'll add a dashboard panel showing per-tenant reconnect rate and a short alert threshold so ops can spot longpoll-induced storms.

oncall_tara: I'll approve a temporary +2x quota bump for tenant-42 until 2025-10-10T02:00:00Z, and set a note on the tenant record. support_jess pls confirm with the customer and get them to deploy client changes.

support_jess: Ack. I told them to implement exponential backoff + increase keepalive to 30s and to respect Retry-After. I also scheduled a call tomorrow to walk through the SDK change. I'll update when they confirm the fix. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: alert summary: tenant-42 429 spike cleared after quota bump at 2025-10-09T00:45Z. peak RPM observed 4200, baseline 800. ongoing watch enabled.

support_jess: closing loop — customer rolled client patch (keepalive -> 30s, jitter/backoff) and errors dropped to <1% window. leaving postmortem note and client SDK PR link in the ticket.
